Package com.nexuslink.protocol.mongo

Record Class MongoShellCommand

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.nexuslink.protocol.mongo.MongoShellCommand
public record MongoShellCommand(String collection, String operation, List<String> arguments, String sort, String projection, Integer limit, Integer skip, boolean count, String unsupportedReason) extends Record
A parsed mongosh-style line: db.<collection>.<operation>(<args>) plus any chained modifiers (.sort(...), .limit(...), .skip(...), .count()).

This is deliberately a grammar parser, not a JavaScript engine. Embedding a JS runtime to run arbitrary shell scripts would be a different product; parsing the call shape covers the way the shell is actually used in a GUI — one statement at a time against one collection — and it fails honestly on anything else instead of half-executing it. unsupportedReason() says so in as many words when a line is beyond the grammar.

Pure: parsing has no connection, so the whole grammar is unit-testable.
